results.title: BBCA and AMRT lead foreign net buying as IHSG falls on Friday (25/6/2026)
results.body: The article reports that PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) and PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT) were the top stocks bought by foreign investors on a day when the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) declined. IHSG closed down 0.9% at 6,241.89 points, a 56‑point drop, marking a 3.09% weekly correction, while foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 559.07 billion on the day and Rp 4.39 trillion over the week. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net purchases were PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Rp 99.03 billion, PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT) Rp 25.73 billion, PT Intermedia Capital Tbk (MDIA) Rp 13.94 billion, PT Karya Pacific Energy Tbk (IATA) Rp 12.87 billion, PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (EMAS) Rp 11.39 billion, PT Bukit Asam Tbk (PTBA) Rp 10.03 billion, PT Bakrie & Brohters Tbk (BNBR) Rp 8.02 billion, PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) Rp 8.02 billion, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) Rp 7.55 billion, and PT Wahana Interfood Nusantara Tbk (COCO) Rp 6.72 billion. These net buying figures show that foreign demand concentrated on these companies despite the broader market’s selling pressure.

results.title: Pilarmas Investindo Sekuritas recommends ADRO, AMRT and SSMS as IHSG faces limited correction
results.body: The article forecasts that the Indonesian composite index (IHSG) will experience limited downside, with support around 6,600 and resistance near 6,710 after closing at 6,636 on September 4, 2026. Pilarmas Investindo Sekuritas points to technical signals and macro conditions—including US‑Iran tensions, OPEC+ production stance and a rise in the 10‑year SBN yield to 7.23% before easing to about 7.1%—as background for its outlook. The brokerage recommends trading the stocks ADRO, AMRT and SSMS on Monday, September 7, 2026.

results.title: MNC Sekuritas recommends AMRT, ELSA, SSMS and INDY as the IHSG targets the 6,705 level
results.body: The article reports that MNC Sekuritas recommends four stocks—AMRT, ELSA, SSMS and INDY—while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) eyes the 6,705 resistance level on 7 September 2026. The IHSG closed at 6,636.47 on Friday, up 0.47% from the prior session and 1.82% (118.35 points) for the week, supported by a net foreign inflow of Rp2.30 trillion and a 35.9% rise in average daily volume to 48.99 billion shares. AMRT fell 1.13% to Rp1,310, ELSA slipped 2.01% to Rp730, SSMS rose 0.42% to Rp1,185, and INDY traded at Rp2,790 with a near‑term correction zone of Rp2,470–Rp2,640 and resistance at its 200‑day moving average (MA200). The market‑wide capitalisation rose 1.47% to Rp11,599 trillion, average daily transaction value increased 25.75% to Rp19.22 trillion, and transaction frequency climbed 10.93% to 2.39 million, underscoring the broader buying pressure behind the index’s potential breakout.

results.title: Analysts Recommend Five Stocks for Correction-Prone Week as IHSG Faces Mixed Outlook
results.body: Analysts from Kiwoom Sekuritas and MNC Sekuritas recommended five stocks for the week of September 7 as the IHSG faces potential correction amid US-Iran tensions and upcoming US inflation data. The IHSG closed at 6,636 on September 4, down 0.47% for the day but up 1.82% for the week, while foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp29.76 billion. Kiwoom's Oktavianus Audi projects the index to move between support 6,575 and resistance 6,718, recommending PT Petrosea Tbk (target 5,950 from 5,375) and PT Timah Tbk (target 4,720 from 4,420). MNC's Herditya Wicaksana sees support at 6,337 and resistance at 6,786, recommending PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (target 1,365 from 1,310), PT Elnusa Tbk (target 830 from 730), and PT Sawit Sumbermas Sarana Tbk (target 1,365 from 1,185).

results.title: Mandiri Sekuritas projects Indonesia's IHSG could reach 7,470 by end‑2026, citing four catalysts
results.body: Mandiri Sekuritas released a broker report on 3 September 2026 projecting the Indonesian composite index (IHSG) to finish 2026 between 5,920 and 7,470, with the index at 6,667 on the day, up 1.09% (72.11 points). Under a base‑case scenario the IHSG is expected at 6,810 with earnings‑per‑share growth of 46%, while a bearish case sees 5,920 and EPS growth of 39%. The report also forecasts the IDX80 to move to 107.2 in the base case, 122.1 in a bullish case and 87.9 in a bearish case, and attributes the outlook to four catalysts: structural gains in precious‑metal, mineral‑downstream and energy sectors; a pro‑people fiscal policy supporting earnings; higher cost of capital prompting more selective investment; and government‑driven industry restructuring encouraging sector rotation. Its top‑10 stock picks are AMMN, ANTM, ARCI, INCO, MEDC, GGRM, AMRT, MIKA, ISAT and BBCA, reflecting expectations that gold, copper, nickel, oil & gas, healthcare, tobacco, telecom and financials will benefit.

results.title: Summary of stock recommendations for 31 August 2026
results.body: The article provides a broker‑compiled list of recommended Indonesian equities for 31 August 2026. It notes that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 6,518.12, down 0.12% on 28 August, with weekly lows of 6,376.65 and sector declines in technology (‑1.95%), transportation (‑1.89%) and property (‑1.62%). The recommended companies are: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas – BBNI, BFIN, VKTR; BNI Sekuritas – CUAN, BRPT, TPIA, ENRG, TAPG, FORE; Phintraco Sekuritas – BBCA, TLKM, DSSA, BBRI, EXCL; Phillip Sekuritas – TSPC, BMRI; MNC Sekuritas – AMRT, BUMI, INDF, LSIP; CGS International Sekuritas – INDY, MDKA, EMAS, BFIN, PWON, MAPA; Panin Sekuritas – MAPI, BBYB, SMRA; Mirae Asset Sekuritas – BBRI, CTRA, ENRG. Trading volume reached 150.03 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp 61.22 trillion across 8.68 million trades.

results.title: Stocks Likely to Gain in Early September Week
results.body: The article provides a broker‑style outlook for Indonesian equities expected to perform well in the first week of September. It notes that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 6,518, down 0.06%, with foreign investors recording a net sell of Rp482.24 billion, setting a cautious market backdrop. Kiwoom Securities Indonesia analyst Oktavianus Audi highlights PT Indika Energy Tbk (INDY) which rose 2.17% to 2,830 and could reach 2,960, and PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR) which jumped 6.63% to 965 with a target of 1,140. MNC Securities analyst Herditya Wicaksana recommends PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT) at 1,340 aiming for 1,520, PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) at 7,300 targeting 7,650, and PT Perusahaan Perkebunan London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) at 1,465 with a projected 1,590. The outlook also references upcoming Indonesian inflation and PMI data, MSCI index rebalancing, and the U.S. Fed’s hawkish tone as broader factors influencing the market.

results.title: OCBC Sekuritas recommends seven undervalued MSCI‑index stocks, including BBCA, with profit potentials up to 61%
results.body: OCBC Sekuritas issued a broker report recommending seven Indonesian MSCI‑index blue‑chip stocks as undervalued opportunities. The report lists PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII), PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (ICBP), PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT) and PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk (MAPI) as buy picks. Target prices are set at Rp8,500 for BBCA, Rp5,500 for BMRI, Rp4,800 for BBNI, Rp7,000 for ASII, Rp10,000 for ICBP, Rp2,200 for AMRT and Rp1,800 for MAPI, implying potential returns of 34%, 32%, 34%, 47%, 30%, 61% and 20% respectively. OCBC also forecasts the IDX Composite (IHSG) to reach 7,800 by end‑2026 supported by a 10% earnings‑growth outlook for listed issuers.

results.title: Retail Stocks Highlighted in Omnichannel Era as AMRT, MIDI and MAPI Gain Analyst Attention
results.body: The article examines analysts’ view that omnichannel strategies are a positive catalyst for Indonesian retail companies. Sucor Sekuritas analyst Christofer Kojongian cites PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk, PT Midi Utama Indonesia Tbk, PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk, PT MAP Aktif Adiperkasa Tbk, PT Aspirasi Hidup Indonesia Tbk and ERAA as having strong membership programs and recommends BUY for AMRT (target Rp1,800), MIDI (Rp410), ERAA (Rp450) and ERAL (Rp330) while assigning HOLD to MAPI (Rp1,400), MAPA (Rp670) and ACES (Rp350). Kiwoom Sekuritas research head Liza Camelia adds that MAPI, ACES and ERAA are well positioned to benefit from omnichannel due to cross‑brand data, home‑living integration and gadget distribution, respectively. Both analysts note that successful digital‑offline integration can improve same‑store sales growth, margins and profitability despite weak consumer purchasing power, with the article dated 19 August 2026.

results.title: Foreign investors quietly amass conglomerate shares, led by Dian Swastatika Sentosa
results.body: Foreign investors accumulated shares of conglomerate and other large‑cap stocks during the week of 10‑14 August 2026 despite an overall net foreign sell of Rp1.58 trillion across the market. Net foreign buying reached Rp21.58 trillion, with the biggest net buy of Rp1.16 trillion in Dian Swastatika Sentosa, followed by Bank Central Asia (Rp380.8 billion) and Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Rp306.6 billion). The top‑10 net‑buy list also includes Timah (Rp222.7 billion), Bank Negara Indonesia (Rp72.1 billion), Aneka Tambang (Rp62.8 billion), Barito Renewables Energy (Rp62.5 billion), J Resources Asia Pasifik (Rp51.7 billion), Sumber Alfaria Trijaya (Rp45.7 billion) and Vale Indonesia (Rp37.8 billion). The broader market slipped, with the IHSG closing down 0.12% at 6,401.89 points, transaction value falling 1.07% to Rp15.21 trillion and traded volume dropping 14.86% to 34.01 billion shares.

results.title: Analyst adds PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk with target Rp1,595 as expansion and cost‑efficiency drive growth despite purchasing‑power pressure
results.body: The article evaluates PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk's growth outlook amid efficiency initiatives and consumer purchasing‑power constraints. AMRT plans to open about 800 new domestic stores—over 50% outside Java—and a total of 1,080 stores including projects in the Philippines and Bangladesh, having opened 167 Alfamart and 42 Alfamidi outlets in the first half of 2026; same‑store sales growth and higher non‑food contribution are highlighted as catalysts. Consensus forecasts revenue growth of roughly 9% and net‑profit growth of about 10% by 2026 with a net margin near 2.7%, while BRI Danareksa projects annual revenue and profit increases of 6.49% and 7.5% respectively; a recent MSCI downgrade to Global Small Cap triggered short‑term foreign outflows but did not alter fundamentals. Mirae Asset analyst Nafan Aji Gusta issues an "add" recommendation with a target price of Rp1,595 per share.

results.title: AMRT EPS Growth Slows as Analysts Adjust Recommendations and Target Prices
results.body: PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk reported a slowdown in earnings per share growth amid weaker consumer purchasing power and higher operating costs, leading analysts to revise their outlooks. The company posted a 6% year‑on‑year revenue increase to Rp 67.95 trillion and net profit of Rp 2.02 trillion (up 8% YoY) for semester I‑2026, while Q2‑2026 net profit rose only 5% YoY to Rp 950 billion and same‑store sales growth decelerated to 2.6%. Operational pressures are compounded by a potential MSCI index downgrade from Global Standard to Global Small Cap, and the subsidiary Lawson is expected to cut its losses to around Rp 150 billion. Analysts from Maybank Sekuritas, Bahana Sekuritas and UBS Global Research kept a buy rating for AMRT with target prices of Rp 2,600, Rp 2,300 and a hold rating with a target of Rp 1,400 respectively.

results.title: MSCI removes PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) from its Global Standard Index and transfers it to the Small Cap Index
results.body: On 13 August 2026 MSCI announced that PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) was taken off the MSCI Global Standard Index and placed into the MSCI Small Cap Index. The move, which occurred alongside the removal of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) and follows the earlier inclusion of PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT), was attributed by Mirae Asset analyst M Nafan Aji Gusta to a significant share‑price decline since the May 2026 review that pushed CPIN's FIF‑adjusted market cap below the Global Standard threshold. On 12 August 2026 CPIN closed up 1.61% at Rp3,150, yet it has corrected 21.84% (‑880 points) over the past three months and is down 30.16% YTD (‑1,360 points).

results.title: Performance of Six Indonesian Companies Removed from the MSCI Main Index
results.body: The article reviews the first‑half‑2026 results of six Indonesian issuers that were taken out of the MSCI Global Standard Index on 13 May 2026. Amman Mineral Intl posted a net profit of US$495.2 million, up 295 % year‑on‑year, driven by higher copper and gold production at Batu Hijau Phase 7. Barito Renewables Energi recorded a net profit of US$61.54 million, a modest 6.2 % increase, while Chandra Asri Pacific posted a net loss of US$38.4 million, a 48.6 % reduction from the prior six‑month loss of US$74.7 million. The remaining three companies—Dian Swastatika Sentosa, Petrindo Jaya Kreasi, and Sumber Alfaria Trijaya—were also removed from the index, though their detailed results were not disclosed in the article.

results.title: Retail investors eye AMRT, HRUM, and ICBP as IHSG poised for limited upside
results.body: Analyst Herditya expects the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) to trade within a narrow range of 6,246 to 6,275 on Wednesday, citing the upcoming MSCI index review and U.S. inflation data. He recommends three stocks for retail investors: PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk with a target price of IDR 1,440‑1,590, PT Harum Energy Tbk with a target of IDR 910‑970, and PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk with a target of IDR 7,800‑8,200. The IHSG had closed down 1.53% at 6,267,880 the previous day, while domestic retail sales contraction narrowed to 3.0% year‑on‑year in June. Geopolitical tension between the United States and Iran and global inflation concerns are noted as broader market influences.

results.title: IHSG Projected to Rebound on 12 August; Analysts Highlight AMRT, HRUM, ICBP, MEDC, ESSA, and WIRG as Buy Targets
results.body: The article forecasts a technical rebound for the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) on Wednesday, 12 August, after a 1.53% decline to 6,267.88 points on Tuesday. Analysts from MNC Sekuritas and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas cite support levels around 6,200‑6,240 and resistance near 6,300‑6,385, with additional support at 6,246 and resistance at 6,275. They recommend buying AMRT at Rp 1,440‑1,590, HRUM at Rp 910‑970, ICBP at Rp 7,800‑8,200, MEDC at Rp 1,370‑1,400, ESSA at Rp 715‑740, and WIRG at Rp 68‑72 per share. The outlook is framed by global factors such as US‑Iran tensions, oil prices, and the upcoming MSCI review, which could influence foreign inflows.

results.title: IHSG predicted to test 6,180‑6,200 support with MNC Sekuritas recommending AMRT, EMAS, HRUM and ICBP for Wednesday trading
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia’s composite index (IHSG) will test the 6,180‑6,200 support level on Wednesday, citing its recent close at 6,267.8, down 1.53% on Tuesday. Phintraco Sekuritas notes the index is below its MA10 but above MA20, while MNC Sekuritas projects a potential rise to 6,440‑6,544 with a correction risk to 5,890‑6,192. MNC Sekuritas recommends trading the stocks AMRT, EMAS, HRUM and ICBP on Wednesday. The outlook is set against a weakening Rupiah at 17,861 per USD (‑0.59%), declining retail sales (‑3% YoY in June) and a 33.3% YoY increase in July car sales to 81,115 units.

results.title: PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk to Open 323 New Alfamart Stores in the First Half of 2026
results.body: PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (Alfamart) announced it will add 323 company‑owned minimarkets in the first half of 2026, raising its owned store count to 15,554 and the total network—including 5,888 franchised outlets—to 21,442 across Indonesia. The expansion lifted its employee base to 98,691, up from 98,515 at the end of 2025. For the semester, the company posted revenue of Rp67.96 trillion, a 6.48 % year‑on‑year increase, with food sales of Rp48.58 trillion and non‑food sales of Rp19.37 trillion. Net profit attributable to the parent grew 7.44 % YoY to Rp2.02 trillion, highlighting the profitability of the store‑growth strategy.

results.title: Technical stock recommendations for ENRG, AADI, and AMRT for Friday, 7 August
results.body: The article provides technical trading recommendations for three Indonesian listed companies—PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk, PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk and PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk—for the session on Friday, 7 August 2026. ENRG closed at Rp 1,430, down 1.04%, and analysts suggest a “Buy on Weakness” between support Rp 1,310 and resistance Rp 1,450. AADI fell to Rp 8,950, down 1.65%; the recommendation is a “Trading Buy” with an entry range of Rp 8,850‑9,000, support Rp 8,700 and resistance Rp 9,800. AMRT ended at Rp 1,400, down 1.75%; analysts advise a “Buy on Break” above Rp 1,440 with a target of Rp 1,520 and a stop‑loss at support Rp 1,375.

results.title: PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk posts net profit of Rp2.02 trillion in H1 2026, up 7.5 % YoY
results.body: The article reports that PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk, the listed issuer of Alfamart stores, recorded net profit of Rp2.02 trillion for the January‑June 2026 period, a 7.5 % increase from the same half‑year in 2025. Consolidated sales rose 6.49 % YoY to Rp67.95 trillion, driven mainly by Rp27.52 trillion of revenue from stores outside Java, with Java and Jabodetabek contributing Rp24.65 trillion and Rp17.43 trillion respectively. Cost of goods sold grew 5.97 % to Rp52.80 trillion and selling, distribution and employee expenses rose modestly, reaching Rp11.91 trillion and Rp6.37 trillion respectively. Total assets reached Rp42.78 trillion, liabilities Rp23.63 trillion and equity Rp19.15 trillion as of June 2026.
